5.7Unified Scale Transformation Record ​

In briefThis record resembles a traceable handover sheet: what object underwent what transformation, what was preserved or lost, how far the evidence supports a conclusion, who may do what, and when stopping is required. A complete form is only a starting point; the substantive materials behind every key reference must also be locatable and checkable.

A scale transformation record is a complete account of one scale transformation. It covers fourteen aspects. Every aspect and every item within it must appear and must not be omitted.

Identity and purpose: which transformation the record concerns, which concept it addresses, which propositions it involves, and what it is for; and which version of the record this is.

Scale: the scale profiles of the source scale and the target scale; the differences on each of the nine axes; which axes are unchanged; the class into which this transformation falls (§5.3); and the state of the scope of authorization, stated as itemized authorizations.

Objects: the effective objects at the source end and the target end; the identity criterion at each end; the identity mapping between the objects at the two ends; and units, population, boundaries, members, and exclusions.

Semantics: the core content that stays the same; the content allowed to change; the content lost; and prohibited mappings.

Transformation: which transformation is evaluated (only one), the selected branch, and the mode of claim (§5.4); the conversion rule; the causal bridge; the time lag; the mapping error; the validity period; the formal test relied on, together with the preselected subtype and success criterion; the positive decision rule and the null-conclusion rule; the positive threshold; the equivalence or sufficiency test; statistical power or sensitivity; the tolerance; and the outcome status.

Variables: inputs, states, outputs, and dependencies between variables.

Evidence: the evidence at the source end and the target end; coverage; heterogeneity; counterexamples; absence signals; alternative explanations; residual tests; and replication or external validation.

Loss: compressed details; irrecoverable information; positions with low visibility; and local exclusion zones.

Responsibility: actors, decision makers, authorizing parties, uptake carriers, responsible parties, beneficiaries, and cost bearers.

Norms: value premises; the type of choice (§14.2); the normative choice record; the normative premises actually adopted this time; the source of authorization; the check under the conclusion rule “Normative Bridging” (§4.14.1); and the four-step operational procedure (§14.6).

Protection: whether protection applies; low-power positions; safe channels for submission; and anti-retaliation.

Action: the judgment ceiling; the action ceiling; prohibited actions; stopping conditions; the responsible person; and the selected action, stated specifically enough to be matched item by item against the approved option.

Correction: appeal, review, restoration, repair, and write-back.

Duration and exit: validity period, review points, suspension, and exit.

Whether the object is preserved, converted, or incomparable across the transformation is determined jointly by three things: the identity criterion at the source end, the identity criterion at the target end, and the identity mapping between the objects at the two ends. A shared name supplies no evidence of identity. An account of the identity mapping must keep all of the following: the main points of each of the two identity criteria; the results of the four checks, that is, whether the source object passes under the source criterion, the source object under the target criterion, the target object under the source criterion, and the target object under the target criterion; the forward and reverse mappings; which criteria were preserved and which were violated; the basis showing that these criteria were pre-registered and finalized before the results were seen; and validation materials that can be reviewed. Each check has only three possible results: passed, failed, and undetermined. A blanket “yes” or “no” must not cover up which check did not pass.

Identity ClassificationMinimum ConditionsCeiling on Conclusions
Same objectThe mappings are valid in both directions. All four checks pass. Some criteria are preserved, and none is violatedThe object’s identity may be retained within the current definition. This does not imply that its semantic, causal, or normative properties are also preserved
Object convertedThe source object passes under the source criterion, the target object passes under the target criterion, and the target object fails under the source criterion. Which items are violated, and what was pre-registered before the results were seen, are both stated specifically. In addition, the mode of claim is object conversion, and there is a supported scale-closure test of the subtype for object or intervention conversion (§4.6)Only an object conversion under the pre-registered identity criteria can be determined. The identity criteria must not be rewritten after the results are seen to manufacture a conversion
IncomparableEach object passes under the criterion of its own end, and at least one cross check (the object at one end under the criterion of the other end) fails. The forward and reverse mappings both keep a complete record of attempts, at least one of which has been shown invalid, with evidence that corresponds to real materialRecords that the two ends are known to be incomparable. The outcome status can only be “not supported or unresolved,” not “not yet evaluated”
UndeterminedThe necessary mappings, criteria, or evidence are still insufficient to complete the classification. Each of the four checks keeps its known “passed” or “failed” result or its still uncertain “undetermined” result, and the check that blocks the overall judgment is identifiedThe outcome status can only be “not supported or unresolved” or “not yet evaluated.” The known parts are not cleared, and an overall “undetermined” is not taken to imply “incomparable” or “object converted”

A determination of object identity must be open to independent recomputation or review by others. The same object under the same criteria can be checked directly. Any other preservation or conversion must retain the objects at both ends, both identity criteria, the direction of the mapping, the results of the four checks, and the supporting materials. A name, a number, a claim of being “valid,” or a mark that identifies material without touching its meaning cannot substitute for this check of meaning.

When the mode of claim is object conversion, the identity classification must agree with the four outcome statuses. Only “supported” corresponds to “object converted.” “Null conclusion supported” corresponds to “same object” when the three null-conclusion criteria (equivalence or sufficiency, statistical power or sensitivity, and tolerance) are all met. “Not supported or unresolved” permits only preservation of the object, a known “incomparable,” or “undetermined.” When the object conversion test has not yet been carried out, the overall classification remains “undetermined,” and any results already checked independently are retained. Neither the absence of a test nor a failed test can therefore justify recording the target in advance as “already converted.” Other modes of claim must not also report “object converted” in the same step. Object conversion must be split off and tested on its own as a separate step.

When the mode of claim is empirical test, causal bridge, object conversion, or intervention conversion, the formal test relied on must be named. The last three must also give a causal bridge, which must not be left empty. Only descriptive mapping may mark the formal test, subtype, and success criterion “not applicable.” For a mode of claim other than descriptive mapping to determine “supported” or “null conclusion supported,” the formal test relied on must also correspond to a real record, and the following must be checked item by item: which test it is, which of the four empirical questions it belongs to, which version of the pre-registration applies, what the preselected subtype and single success criterion are, and what status the test itself is in. A name or number that merely looks correctly formatted cannot stand in for a test. A descriptive bridge may be recorded as “supported” if it meets the positive criterion. Record “not yet evaluated” only when the selected mode of claim has not yet been carried out.

The fourteen aspects form a stable framework; they do not project the meanings of human governance onto every object. Whether protection applies must be stated explicitly, with the object type, downstream use, rationale, and evidence. It must not be inferred from the fact that a list such as the list of actors is empty. An object may be nonhuman, with its use limited to two kinds: description only, or a nonhuman intervention shown by evidence to have no effect on humans or sentient beings. In that case, the two items of safe submission and anti-retaliation may be marked “not applicable,” with reasons stated. Real-world experimental or engineering interventions, however, still have an acting subject and an object. The specific authorization, the person responsible for the action, and the arrangements for stopping, review, and restoration must be stated. Only purely descriptive use allows the axis of jurisdiction and authorization to be inapplicable. Energy, matter, or computational resources in a natural system do not by themselves trigger these requirements for protecting people. When the object is human, sentient nonhuman, mixed, or unknown, or the use concerns the evaluation of people, the allocation of their scarce resources, their rights, their exposure to risk, or real-world action involving them, the items of protection immediately become content that must be accounted for. An earlier “not applicable” must not carry over. The inapplicability of protection never implies that action is justified. Normative choice still requires a separate judgment.

The person responsible for the action specifies only who is responsible for carrying out or stopping it. Having such a person provides no basis for inferring that the mode of claim is intervention conversion, nor does it establish that the action is effective or justified. Every external action must correspond to a normative choice record (see Part 14) and disclose its value premises and the normative premises actually adopted this time. The normative premise “Explanation Does Not Confer Authority to Act” (§14.3) can by itself only block actions that exceed authorization. It cannot generate an affirmative option. The feasible options in the choice record are not a list of names but options whose content is set down. For each option, its kind, action type, target object, geographic area, validity period, reversibility, expected impacts, and distributional impacts are fixed in advance, and the options explicitly include one no-action option. The selected action must correspond to one of the external-action options and must match it item by item on action, object, geographic area, and validity period. All three of the following must be rejected: pointing in fact to the no-action option while using it as the basis for an external action; matching only the name in words while the content does not match item by item; and rewriting both the action and the authorization while the approved option remains unchanged. There must also be at least one currently valid, independently reviewed itemized authorization that covers this subject, object, action, geographic area, and period together and agrees with the stated source of authorization. An authorization unrelated to this action cannot back the proposed action, even if it is formally valid. The record must also have the following: the ten components that “Normative Bridging” requires, all of them passed; the records of each step of the four-step operational procedure; the person responsible for the action; prohibited actions; and the arrangements for stopping, protection, appeal, review, and restoration. If any item is missing, the action ceiling can only be taking no action or continuing deliberation. Whether an intervention conversion has occurred empirically is judged separately by the relevant formal test.

Joining several transformation steps one after another only sets the order of composition. Support gained at one step does not automatically carry to the next. Checking such a chain must ensure that each step has its own separate record, not confused with other steps; that each step contains only one transformation; that the objects and identity criteria referred to by adjacent steps are compatible; and that the target scale of each step matches the source scale of the next. If any step is unresolved, becomes invalid, or exceeds its loss limit, this must be retained in the conclusion for the whole chain. Success at the final step cannot override it.

Evaluation of the whole chain must also state whether the final task is consistent with the tasks at the individual steps and whether shared resources have been committed more than once. Two tasks can each be feasible with one unit of capacity and yet be impossible to complete together if they share that unit in the same period. If time limits, resources, or permitted strategies are legitimately changed, the new joint option should be evaluated. Representational sufficiency, joint causal response, and joint resource feasibility each have their own criteria. Passing one cannot substitute for passing the other two.

5.7Note

Understanding this section

5.7 Unified scale-transformation record

This record resembles a traceable handover sheet: what object underwent what transformation, what was preserved or lost, how far the evidence supports a conclusion, who may do what, and when stopping is required. A complete form is only a starting point; the substantive materials behind every key reference must also be locatable and checkable.

The fourteen aspects form a stable framework; choosing a few familiar columns does not make a record complete. The items connect objects, representations, evidence, norms, and actual action while preserving their distinctions. Each aspect is explained below in the order of the original text; even inapplicability requires explicit reasons, and unknowns cannot be hidden in empty lists.

① Identity and purpose: state which transformation this record concerns, which concept it addresses, which propositions being tested or used it involves, what it is for, and which version of the record this is. Similar names, the same formatting, or an unchanged version cannot replace consistency of the actual object and claim. When the purpose changes from description to action upon an object, subsequent responsibilities must be reviewed again.

② Scale: fully state the scale profiles of source scale SP0 and target scale SP1, the differences on each of the nine axes, which axes are unchanged, the class into which this transformation falls, and the state of the scope of authorization, stated as itemized authorizations. Even unchanged axes require explanations of why they are equal; unknowns and incomparability must be retained under the rules in 5.3, rather than hiding mixed changes behind an ‘upscaling’ label. The scope of authorization can be established only through corresponding valid authorization, not carried along by expansion of the other eight axes.

③ Objects: preserve valid source/target objects, the identity criterion at each end, the identity mapping between the objects at the two ends, and units, populations, boundaries, members, and exclusions. The identity criterion is the object criterion used here, not an alias that can be changed with the results. The mapping must let others see the objects at both ends, both identity criteria, the forward and reverse directions, and each criterion, rather than merely saying ‘same’.

④ Semantics: “the core content that stays the same” explains the core that must be retained, “the content allowed to change” declares what may change, “the content lost” lists what was lost, and “prohibited mappings” specifies what it must not be recast as. Preservation and loss can coexist—for example, preserving the total while losing individual order; ‘the core is unchanged’ cannot conceal losses needed for the task.

⑤ Transformation: state the single transformation, the selected branch and mode of claim, the conversion rule, causal bridge, time lag, mapping error, validity period, the formal test relied on, subtype, unique success criterion, the positive decision rule and the null-conclusion rule, positive threshold, equivalence/sufficiency tests, power/sensitivity, tolerance, and outcome status. Each answers a distinct question; the name of the transformation does not determine the status, and failing the positive criterion does not automatically create null support. Items in a descriptive mapping that belong only to empirical tests may be inapplicable with reasons, but the descriptive bridge and evaluation cannot therefore be omitted.

⑥ Variables: list inputs, states, outputs, and cross-variable dependencies, specifying which quantities are measured, controlled, aggregated, or inferred. Variable names alone are insufficient for checking causation or computation; whether a dependency is definitional, statistical association, or an effect relation must be expressed clearly for the present claim.

⑦ Evidence: list source and target evidence separately, together with coverage, heterogeneity, counterexamples, absence signals, alternative explanations, residual tests, replication, or external validation. Absence signals can be meaningful only with adequate observational capacity and windows; lacking materials and observing absence are different. Reprocessing materials from the same source does not create independent sources.

⑧ Loss: disclose compression details, unrecoverable information, positions with low visibility, and local exclusion zones. Traceability of the object as a whole does not mean every member remains visible; sufficiency of a representation for one task does not mean losslessness for all uses. State precisely which conclusion or action each loss blocks.

⑨ Responsibility: separately list actors, decision-makers, authorizers, uptake carriers, responsible parties, beneficiaries, and cost bearers. A database can carry traces without thereby becoming a person bearing moral/legal responsibility; beneficiaries need not be decision-makers, and cost bearers should not be concealed by population averages.

⑩ Norms: disclose value premises, choice type, the normative choice record, the normative premises actually adopted this time, authorization sources, the check under “Normative Bridging” (§4.14.1), and the four-step operational procedure (§14.6). Facts or technical feasibility cannot choose objectives on their own; the normative premise “Explanation Does Not Confer Authority to Act” only prevents overreach and cannot alone generate a positive proposal. Analysis for deliberation may retain recommendation status, but actual adoption must complete the choice and action conditions specified here.

⑪ Protection: explicitly state applicability, low-power positions, safe submission, and protection against retaliation. Applicability itself requires object type, downstream use, reasons, and evidence references; an empty list of actors cannot imply that protection is unnecessary. This describes when safeguards must activate, rather than attaching human-governance terminology indiscriminately to every natural process.

⑫ Action: separate the judgment ceiling from the action ceiling and list prohibited actions, stopping conditions, responsible people, and the selected action, stated specifically enough to be matched item by item against the approved option. Evidence supporting a description does not confer authority to act. The person responsible for the action denotes only responsibility for execution or stopping; it does not imply that the mode of claim is intervention conversion or establish an action's effects or normative justification.

⑬ Correction: appeal, review, restoration, repair, and write-back must each be accessible. An appeal entry point is not a completed review, and a promise to repair is not a recovered object; specify who performs the work and how completion is checked, while preserving past versions and failures.

⑭ Duration and exit: record the validity period, review points, suspension, and exit. A record passing in the past does not guarantee continued applicability after conditions change; expiry or a stopping condition should trigger invalidation/review under the procedure, not extension of authority by reusing the number.

At minimum, an object mapping must preserve the main points of both identity criteria, four three-valued checks, bidirectional mappings, preserved/violated criteria, the basis showing that the criteria were pre-registered and finalized before the results, and validation materials that can be reviewed. The four checks are the source object under the source criterion, the source object under the target criterion, the target object under the source criterion, and the target object under the target criterion; each may be only passed, failed, or undetermined. A mark that only identifies material helps recognize the same material; it does not establish the correctness of semantic judgments within it.

“Same object” requires valid mappings in both directions, all four checks passed, some criteria preserved, and none violated. It permits continuation of identity only within the current definition, without implying preservation of semantics, causation, norms, authority, or every task.

“Object converted” requires the source object to pass under the source criterion and the target object under the target criterion, and the target object to fail under the source criterion; violated items and the pre-registration basis from before the results must be specific. It must additionally use the mode of claim of object conversion and have a supported scale-closure test of the subtype for object or intervention conversion. Changing the identity criterion after results to manufacture ‘conversion’ is prohibited; a single failed cross-check is also insufficient for this classification.

“Incomparable” requires each endpoint to pass under its own criterion, at least one failed cross-check, complete records of attempts at both mapping directions with at least one validation invalid, and evidence that corresponds to real material. This is known incomparability, not lack of evaluation, and the result may only be “not supported or unresolved.”

“Undetermined” means necessary mappings, criteria, or evidence are insufficient; known “passed” or “failed” values remain recorded item by item, with the exact item blocking overall classification identified. The result may only be “not supported or unresolved” or “not yet evaluated.” Overall uncertainty cannot be spread into four unknown checks, nor may an unknown be treated as incomparability or conversion.

Under the mode of claim of object conversion, only “supported” corresponds to “object converted”; “null conclusion supported” must correspond to “same object” and pass all three null-conclusion criteria; “not supported or unresolved” permits only identity preservation, known incomparability, or “undetermined.” When the test has not been carried out, the overall classification is “undetermined,” while independently checked local results remain preserved. Other modes of claim must not simultaneously report “object converted” in the same step; conversion requires its own separate step and test.

Empirical test, causal bridge, object conversion, and intervention conversion all require naming the formal test relied on; the latter three additionally require a nonempty causal bridge. Only descriptive mapping may mark the formal test, subtype, and success criterion “not applicable.” For a mode of claim other than descriptive mapping to determine “supported” or “null conclusion supported,” the test relied on must also correspond to a real record, checking which test it is, which of the four empirical questions it belongs to, which version of the pre-registration applies, the preselected subtype, the unique criterion, and the status of this test; a name or number that merely resembles a scale-closure test is insufficient. A descriptive bridge that passed positively can be “supported”; “not yet evaluated” is recorded only when the selected mode of claim has not been carried out.

Protection inapplicability is limited to an explicitly nonhuman object whose use is either description only or a nonhuman intervention shown by evidence to have no effect on humans or sentient beings; in those cases the two items of safe submission and anti-retaliation may be inapplicable with reasons. Energy, matter, or computing resources in natural systems do not themselves trigger requirements for protecting people. Even when the preceding nonhuman-intervention conditions hold, actual engineering/experimentation still requires specific authorization, a person responsible for the action, stopping, review, and restoration; only pure description permits the axis of jurisdiction and authorization to be inapplicable.

If the object is human, sentient nonhuman, mixed, or unknown, or the use involves evaluating people, allocating scarce resources, rights, exposure risks, or actual action upon objects, the items of protection immediately become content that must be accounted for. A change in downstream use reopens the applicability judgment; an earlier descriptive inapplicability cannot be inherited. Protection inapplicability itself also does not establish that an action is justified; value choices still require explanation.

Every external action must correspond to a normative choice record and disclose value premises and the normative premises actually adopted this time. Feasible options are not a list of names but options whose content is set down; each fixes the kind of option, action type, target object, jurisdiction, validity period, reversibility, expected effects, and distributional effects. The options explicitly include one no-action option, making ‘no action’ an actual comparable option.

The selected action must correspond to one of the external-action options, with action, object, jurisdiction, and validity period matching the approved option item by item. Pointing to the no-action option, matching only a name in words, or changing the action and the authorization together without changing the approved option must be rejected. At least one currently valid, independently reviewed itemized authorization must simultaneously cover the same subject, object, action, jurisdiction, and period and agree with the authorization source; an unrelated valid permit is insufficient, and items from several permits cannot be cross-spliced.

Normative bridging (§4.14.1) requires ten components: descriptive or explanatory conclusions; current evidence and epistemic constraints; explicit normative premises; the record of normative conflicts; the status of the protection floor; the record of authorization and jurisdiction; options including no action; the records of the operational procedure; the action ceiling; and stopping, review, restoration, and remedy. It is a check on the validity of the bridge, not a substitute for people's value choices. The first step, “Fixing the Facts and Evidence,” fixes descriptions and evidence; the second, “Stating the Normative Premises and Conflicts,” discloses normative premises and conflicts; the third, “Reviewing Authorization and Comparing Options,” checks authorization and options; and the fourth, “Bounded Execution and Correction,” arranges bounded execution, monitoring, stopping, and correction.

External action additionally requires the ten components of normative bridging, all passed, the records of each step of the four-step operational procedure, a person responsible for the action, prohibited actions, stopping, protection, appeal, review, and restoration. If any required item is missing, the action ceiling is limited to no action or continued deliberation. Satisfying these procedures does not establish empirical intervention conversion; that remains a judgment for the corresponding formal test.

Every step in a record chain has its own separate record and only one transformation; adjacent object references and identity criteria are compatible, and the target scale of the earlier step matches the source scale of the later one. Each step's unresolved status, failure, and losses beyond limits must enter the chain-level report and cannot be overwritten by success at the final step. A chain only sets the sequence; connecting lines do not transmit support.

Chain-level checks must additionally verify the same final task and whether shared resources are committed more than once. Representational sufficiency for the task, joint responses to combined interventions, and joint feasibility under common resources have different criteria. If two tasks each require one unit and total resources are one unit, each being feasible alone does not imply simultaneous feasibility in the same period. After a legitimate change to the horizon, resources, or permitted strategies, evaluate the new joint plan rather than retrospectively declaring the old one feasible.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Build an item-by-item record across the fourteen aspects, first fixing use, version, the object's identity criterion, single transformation, branch, and mode of claim.

  2. 2

    State the scale profiles and their differences axis by axis, specifying preservation, permitted changes, losses, and prohibited mappings.

  3. 3

    Place both objects under both identity criteria for four three-valued checks, preserve bidirectional mapping attempts and reviewable material, then determine the overall classification.

  4. 4

    Check compatibility among the mode of claim, the formal test relied on, the preselected criterion, and the outcome status; a name or number cannot fill the absence of a substantive test.

  5. 5

    Assess protection applicability by object and downstream use; actual nonhuman intervention still requires checking the acting subject and specific authorization.

  6. 6

    Set down the content of all options and retain one no-action option; the selected action must correspond exactly and match item by item.

  7. 7

    Independently check that one complete itemized authorization simultaneously covers the proposed action, and check the normative premises, the ten components of normative bridging, the four-step operational procedure, and correction conditions.

  8. 8

    If required action conditions are missing, remain with no action or further deliberation; empirical support cannot expand action eligibility.

  9. 9

    For multiple steps, check adjacent objects/scale profiles and preserve each step’s result and loss, then separately test final representation, joint response, and resource constraints.

  10. 10

    After execution or a change of use, conduct life-cycle review, preserving original versions, stopping, and actual repair records.

Distinctions to keep clear

Complete items

All required items and references are present.

≠

Substantive validity

Mappings, tests, facts, norms, and authority each have checkable grounds.

Same object

Identity preserved under the current identity criterion.

≠

Preservation of all properties

Semantics, causation, norms, and tasks still require separate checking.

Known incomparability

Complete mapping attempts and cross-checks supply evidence of invalidity.

≠

Overall unresolved status

Necessary materials are still missing; preserve each item's known value.

Person responsible for the action

Who executes or stops.

≠

Action permission and empirical conversion

Judged respectively through choice/authorization procedures and test evidence.

Protection inapplicable for pure description

A bounded status with an explicit object, use, and reasons.

≠

Real-world intervention without responsibility

This does not follow; actual interventions still require authorization, responsibility, and correction.

Success at each step

Each step passes its own task or rules.

≠

Chain-level success

The same final task, joint response, and resources all require further checking.

Mathematical construction: bidirectional preservation gives only current identity qualificationTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe object is explicitly an abstract graph-isomorphism class, both identity criteria are fixed before results, and mapping and inverse are checked edge by edge; this is not an empirical formal test.

Take an abstract unlabeled three-vertex path as the object. Fix the identity criteria at both the source end and the target end as ‘exactly three vertices, two edges, degree sequence 1/2/1; graph isomorphism identifies the same abstract object’. Source labels are {1,2,3} with edges {12,23}; target labels are {a,b,c} with edges {ab,bc}. Mapping 1→a,2→b,3→c and its inverse are both bijective and edge-preserving; all four identity checks pass, some criteria are preserved, and there are no violations. Under this teaching identity criterion, the object may be judged “same object.” This does not say that two actual sheets of paper are the same physical object or judge the causality or authority of these edges.

BoundaryIdentity depends on the declared identity criterion; labeled-object or physical-artifact identity requires renewed checks.

Teaching construction: overall uncertainty retains local knowledgeTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe four values and material gaps are fictional assumptions; no actual test or verification credential was created.

Let the source object under the source criterion be “passed,” the source object under the target criterion “undetermined,” the target object under the source criterion “failed,” and the target object under the target criterion “passed”; verification material for the reverse mapping is still absent. The material cannot complete the overall classification: retain these four values and gaps, with overall “undetermined.” One failed cross-check cannot establish “object converted,” nor may an overall undetermined state turn a known failure into “unknown.” Establishing a known “incomparable” still requires complete bidirectional attempts and at least one invalid verification, among other conditions; “object converted” additionally requires this section’s mode of claim of object conversion and a supported scale-closure test of the subtype for object or intervention conversion.

BoundaryThis illustrates the conditions for classification and claims neither that the fictional object conversion occurred nor that a mechanism is absent.

Teaching construction: options fixed in advance and actions matched exactlyTeaching scenario

AssumptionsAll numbers, slider, window, and authorization assumptions are teaching symbols; no actual authorization, choice record, check under normative bridging, or execution permit was obtained or fabricated. This checks only the consistency of the items and does not claim that other action conditions passed.

In a fictional experiment, option N0 is the no-action option: keep slider S in position, on workbench B, in single window W; reversibility involves no state change, the expected impact is no new movement, and the distributional impact is none. Option A1 is an external-action option: move S from 0 to 1 on workbench B during W, reversible by returning to 0; only position is expected to change, with corresponding material confirming no effects on human risk/resource distribution. The listed no-action option is N0. If the selected action points to A1 but the actual description says ‘move to 2’, even a valid authorization covering movement to 2 does not match the approved A1. The option must be reconsidered rather than proceeding after only changing the authorization. Likewise reject movement when N0 is selected.

BoundaryAbsence of risk in a nonhuman case requires evidence, not a verbal assumption; actual experiments still need specific authorization, responsibility, stopping, review, restoration, and all other required conditions.

Mathematical construction: separately feasible tasks cannot share a single unit of capacityTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe resource cannot be shared simultaneously, has no substitute source, and same-period completion is fixed; two-period reuse is separately specified as changed conditions.

A fictional same-period resource total is C=1; tasks A and B each need 1, cannot share the same unit, and must finish in the same period. A alone satisfies 1≤1 and B alone also satisfies 1≤1; jointly they need 1+1=2>1 and are infeasible. Only if deadlines permit two periods and the resource can be fully reused each period can a new proposal of A followed by B be studied; that does not make the old simultaneous proposal feasible.

BoundaryThis proves only a resource constraint, not joint intervention effects or sufficiency of the final representation.

Mathematical construction: completing every stage’s task can still lose the final queryTeaching scenario

AssumptionsA complete binary domain, deterministic mappings, and the original final task fixed before results; no actual personal data are involved.

The first step preserves a binary pair (x₁,x₂) completely; the second outputs only its sum. The first preservation task and second counting task may both be exact, yet if the original final q is the first coordinate x₁, (0,1) and (1,0) both become 1 while their answers differ, so the final task fails. Adding the first-coordinate label can repair this task, but resources and authorization still require separate checks.

BoundaryProof of representational composition does not replace joint causal responses or implementation resources.

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleSource and target share a name and are checked to be the same file, so identity, semantics, causality, and authority are all declared preserved.

What it limitsFinding that it is the same file identifies only the material; the four identity checks and other claims still require separate checks.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

Teaching counterexampleThe human-participant list is empty, so protection and the scope of authorization are both marked inapplicable and equipment adjustments are implemented.

What it limitsProtection applicability must be explicit by type/use and evidence; actual engineering actions still require specific authorization and other conditions.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

Teaching counterexampleOption A was approved for object X; the action and authorization are changed to object Y while A’s choice record is reused.

What it limitsThe approved option’s object does not match; changing two items together cannot bypass choice.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

Teaching counterexampleA mode of claim other than descriptive mapping writes only a name or number that looks like a test of object or intervention conversion and is marked “supported.”

What it limitsSuch a name or number cannot replace a test that corresponds to a real record, its version, subtype, criterion, status, and actual evidence.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

Teaching counterexampleSuccess in the chain’s last step deletes uncertainty in its first step.

What it limitsThe chain must retain every step’s unresolved state, failure, and excessive loss; final success has no authority to overwrite them.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • Names, numbers, self-claimed statuses, and marks that only identify material do not replace semantic verification; a reference that matches the material does not guarantee its contents are true.
  • If only three checks are known to pass and one is unknown, “same object” must not be recorded; overall uncertainty also cannot erase the three known checks.
  • If the conversion test has not been carried out or has not passed, the target cannot first be named “object converted.”
  • Modes of claim other than descriptive mapping must name the formal test relied on, but writing down just any name or number does not qualify; support statuses must actually correspond to real records and be compatible.
  • Unknown object type makes protection mandatory; failure to find people cannot default to absence of human effects.
  • Unrelated authorizations, cross-splicing items, or changing the action and the authorization together cannot bypass exact matching to the approved option.
  • No action is one of the options; it cannot be used as the basis for an external action while execution continues.
  • The same resource cannot be promised twice in one period; added resources or extended deadlines are conditions of a new proposal.
  • All record examples in this guide are teaching checks, not executable authorizations, formal tests, or real proposals that have passed normative bridging.

Scope and open questions

This section specifies unified recording and type/state consistency. Explicit formal examples and teaching checks show the reasoning; no complete real case covering the fourteen aspects exists to award a state here, so historical material is not forced into an execution record marked passed.

If one of the four identity checks is unknown and three pass, may “same object” be recorded?

No. “Same object” requires all four checks to pass, valid bidirectional mappings, and other conditions; retain known passes and overall gaps.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Is the target object’s failure to satisfy the source criterion enough to record “object converted”?

No. Both endpoints must also pass under their own criteria, with specific violated items and the pre-registration basis, the mode of claim of object conversion, a supported scale-closure test of the subtype for object or intervention conversion, and other conditions.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If safe submission under protection is inapplicable, does an actual nonhuman experiment need no specific authorization?

Specific authorization, action responsibility, stopping, review, and restoration remain necessary; only purely descriptive use permits the axis of jurisdiction and authorization to be inapplicable.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If the selected action points to the no-action option but the action description says repair, may it be executed?

No. An external action must correspond to an external-action option and match the approved option item by item; the no-action option cannot be used to carry out an action.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Why might one valid permit still be insufficient?

One itemized authorization must simultaneously cover this subject, object, action, territory, and period, agree with its source, and leave no other action condition missing.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Does having an execution owner mean that this is intervention conversion?

No. An owner is a responsibility arrangement; intervention conversion is a separate claim requiring an empirical test and evidence.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If two tasks each need 1 and total capacity is 1, why do individual passes not permit joint execution in the same period?

Joint demand 2 exceeds total 1, double-promising resources; phasing is a new proposal requiring separate evaluation.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Can “Explanation Does Not Confer Authority to Act” and complete items automatically select the optimal action?

No. “Explanation Does Not Confer Authority to Act” only prevents overreach; explicit positive normative premises, option comparisons, normative bridging, operational procedures, authorization, and other conditions are necessary. A table does not replace value choice.

5.8Consistency Checks and the Protection Floor ​

In briefA machine can check a table’s consistency without thereby guaranteeing that the world described in it is true. In particular, ‘unknown’, ‘unobservable’, ‘inapplicable’, and ‘protectively undisclosed’ cannot all be compressed into zero and then used to decide for people.

A consistency check deals only with formal matters: whether the items, references, versions, and outcome statuses are consistent with one another, and whether the recorded axis relations have been combined correctly. It cannot replace the judgments that substantive comparisons in each domain make about geometry, organizational graphs, causal abstraction, network embedding, object identity, or authorization validity. Without substantive comparisons and independent materials about the objects, a complete record or algorithmic output cannot justify determining scale elevation. A record may take any form, but it must meet the same requirements for traceability and review.

The four missingness statuses form a closed set, to which nothing else is added. “Unknown” means that it is not yet known. “Not applicable” means that it genuinely does not apply under the definition. “Unobservable” means that it cannot be observed through the current channel and within the current time window. “Withheld for protection” means that it is not disclosed in order to protect. None of the four means “absent,” and deleting the item cannot substitute for marking its status.

Uptake carriers and responsible parties must be written down separately. Taking something up, being visible, being affected, or having greater capability does not by itself create responsibility. Whenever there is an effect on the rights of humans or sentient subjects, on the allocation of their scarce resources, on their exposure to risk, or on how they are treated in practice, the protection floor (§14.8) must identify low-power positions and local exclusion zones. It must provide arrangements for safe submission, anti-retaliation, stopping, appeal, review, and restoration. In these cases, it must not be marked “not applicable.” Insufficient protection lowers both the judgment ceiling and the action ceiling. A purely descriptive record may, under certain conditions, mark protection “not applicable,” but downstream actions cannot carry over that inapplicability. Once the use changes, the protection review must be reopened.

5.8Note

Understanding this section

5.8 Consistency Checks and the Protection Floor

A machine can check a table’s consistency without thereby guaranteeing that the world described in it is true. In particular, ‘unknown’, ‘unobservable’, ‘inapplicable’, and ‘protectively undisclosed’ cannot all be compressed into zero and then used to decide for people.

A consistency check mainly checks complete items, references that match, compatible versions, nonconflicting outcome statuses, and rule-compliant combination of existing nine-axis relations. It can find missing items, incorrect references, illegal states, and wrong combination order, but these checks do not themselves establish correct inputs on each axis.

Geometric containment, organizational-chart relations, causal abstraction, network embedding, object identity, and valid authorization are responsibilities of domain comparison. Domain comparators may themselves be programs, but require corresponding semantics, object material, algorithm applicability conditions, and reviewable grounds. ‘A machine also calculated it’ or ‘the program passed’ cannot remove this responsibility. Without substantive comparison and independent object material, scale elevation cannot be determined on the strength of a complete record.

The four missingness statuses form a closed set: “unknown” means not currently known; “not applicable” means genuinely inapplicable under the definition; “unobservable” means unobservable through current channels and window; “withheld for protection” means not disclosed in order to protect. They explain different reasons and none means the fact does not exist. Deleting the item also deletes the gap’s status and is not a fifth legitimate treatment.

These labels are not exemption buttons. “Not applicable” needs a reason from the definition/use; “unobservable” must explain channel and window restrictions; protective nondisclosure requires protective grounds and proportionate review arrangements. Retaining a protective state does not require revealing sensitive content to fill a table, nor does absent public content mean absent evidence or affected people.

Uptake carriers and responsible parties must be written down separately. Servers or files can carry information; people can be visible, affected, or more capable. None of these relations independently creates responsibility. Responsibility requires separate examination of actual participation, decisions, commitments, rules, and corresponding norms; record keepers or affected people do not automatically become responsible for an outcome.

Whenever rights of humans or sentient subjects, scarce-resource allocation, exposure risks, or actual action upon them are affected, identify low-power positions and local exclusion zones and provide safe submission, anti-retaliation, stopping, appeal, review, and restoration. These cannot be labeled inapplicable, and naming a hotline alone does not establish actually usable protection.

Insufficient protection lowers both judgment and action ceilings. Unsafe expression may limit material coverage and visibility of counterexamples, preventing claims to comprehensive knowledge; actions likewise cannot keep expanding. Lowering ceilings does not declare every known local fact false; it specifies which stronger judgments and actions the present material and protections cannot support.

Reasoned inapplicability for a purely descriptive use does not automatically transfer to downstream action. When use changes from statistical description to evaluating people’s eligibility, allocating resources, or taking action upon them, reopen protection review and return to 5.7’s conditions for choice, authorization, responsibility, and correction. A record may take different formats, but traceability and review responsibilities cannot diminish.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    First distinguish structure/reference/state/combination checks from domain-semantic comparison; successful validation cannot testify across these levels.

  2. 2

    For every axis relation, check actual object material, comparator definition, applicability domain, and grounds for the result.

  3. 3

    Use one of the four states for every missing item and explain the reason; do not compress missingness into nonexistence or simply delete it.

  4. 4

    Separate uptake carriers from responsible parties, specifying grounds of responsibility and unknowns independently.

  5. 5

    Assess protection triggers by object and downstream use, identifying low-power and excluded positions.

  6. 6

    Check whether safe submission, anti-retaliation, and stopping/appeal/review/restoration are reachable, rather than checking names alone.

  7. 7

    When protections are insufficient, narrow both judgment and action ceilings while retaining still-valid local facts.

  8. 8

    Reopen review when use changes; an execution record cannot inherit inapplicability from an old descriptive record.

Distinctions to keep clear

Structural validation

Checks compliance with type, reference, and combination rules.

≠

Domain judgment

Checks whether object relations and evidence substantively satisfy semantic conditions.

Unknown

Insufficient information currently to determine.

≠

Unobservable

Current channels and window cannot observe it: a more specific reason.

Not applicable

Genuinely inapplicable under this definition and use.

≠

Withheld for protection

Undisclosed for protection, not inherently inapplicable.

Uptake carrier

Where information, states, or effects are retained.

≠

Responsible party

Who bears which responsibilities on factual and normative grounds.

Lower ceilings

Limit stronger conclusions and actions.

≠

All facts invalidated

Not an automatic consequence of insufficient protection.

Mathematical construction: the combination algorithm is correct while axis inputs may be wrongTeaching scenario

AssumptionsComplete finite sets with unambiguous membership. A's other items, including partition, unit mapping, weights, and comparison rules, are complete and compatible; mutual noninclusion alone excludes coverage in either direction. Equality of the other eight axes is a teaching assumption. No actual authorization is simulated.

Let source membership set S={a,b} and target T={b,c,d}, with the other eight axes assumed adequately supported as “equal.” If A is incorrectly labeled with the valid value “expands,” combining under the rules of §5.3 yields “scale elevation,” and the combination may be entirely correct. But a∉T, so T does not cover S; c,d∉S as well, making the sets mutually noninclusive. A should be incomparable under the relevant membership-comparison conditions. Restoring the correct A changes the product-relation classification to “horizontal or incomparable.”

BoundaryDemonstrates separate responsibilities for semantic inputs and composition, not that an actual system has been labeled incorrectly.

Teaching construction: four empty values require four different reasonsTeaching scenario

AssumptionsLetters denote fictional samples with no actual health or privacy information. Labels follow the stipulated definition, window, and protective grounds.

A fictional record asks whether a sample was exposed to condition E. A's measurement has not returned: “unknown.” B's task, as defined, does not involve E: “not applicable.” C's sensing channel cannot detect E within the specified window: “unobservable.” D's relevant information cannot be disclosed for protection: “withheld for protection.” None means “unexposed,” and none may be deleted to treat the remaining samples as complete coverage.

BoundaryLater changes in use or evidence require status review. This example does not require disclosure of D's information.

Teaching construction: descriptive use becomes allocative useTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe project and scoring are constructed, without actual lists, authorization, or allocation actions.

A fictional project initially only summarizes unmanned-simulator logs, marking human protections such as safe submission inapplicable for explicit object/use reasons. Someone later proposes using the score to determine actual people's access to scarce training places. This new use involves human evaluation and resource allocation, immediately reopening protection review. The original inapplicability cannot be copied. Even correct technical scoring does not remove the need to check normative premises, authorization, and procedures for the allocation plan.

BoundaryIllustrates a change in downstream use; it offers neither personnel-selection advice nor a legitimacy determination.

Missing addresses on Snow’s map do not mean the corresponding cases do not existDocumented case

In his map explanation, Snow writes that the original addresses of some people who died after transfer to hospitals or relief institutions were unrecorded or only partly recovered. These address gaps limit mapping but do not erase known deaths. This section adds the observation that missing states cannot be compressed into negation, without rejecting the map’s bounded use for geographic distribution.

SourceJohn Snow（1855）Printed pp. 45–46, first paragraph explaining MAP 1 and the subsequent qualification of its topographical useReading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsSupports the original author’s disclosed address gaps and use limits; it does not retrospectively assign modern four-state labels to every historical gap or declare the whole map invalid.

What does not follow

  • This does not claim that machines can never perform domain comparisons; those comparisons themselves must bear semantic, evidentiary, and review responsibilities.
  • Protective nondisclosure cannot be treated as noncooperation to compel exposure; judgments should respect its support scope and safe-review conditions.
  • Unknown cannot automatically become inapplicable; when type is unknown, an empty list cannot disable protections.
  • Incorrect inputs can make a correct combination algorithm produce false real-world conclusions; locate input responsibilities rather than rejecting all algorithms wholesale.
  • This section’s teaching table is not an actual personnel-evaluation system, and no real data collection or protection testing was implemented.

Scope and open questions

The original work explicitly distinguishes known events from missing locations, illustrating why missingness cannot become nonexistence. Modern labels serve only this section's explanation and do not retroactively claim that the historical records already used this set of labels.

5.9Evidence Boundaries and Independent Support ​

In briefLabeling a transformation “Aggregation” or “Compression or Abstraction” states only which rules will guide the question. The target object's properties require its own material; source-object success or procedural self-claims cannot fill the gaps.

The names, numbers, summaries of meaning, and classifications of the nine scale transformations specify only how a transformation should be described and tested. They provide no empirical support that the transformation occurred, the mapping is valid, or the target property holds. Concept labels internal to the framework, examples, how completely the items are filled in, and results reported by the algorithm itself must not serve as evidence at the source end or the target end in place of materials about the objects.

Every actual transformation must obtain independent, verifiable materials separately for the source object and the target object. It must state the mapping, what is preserved, changed, or lost, the error, and the competing explanations, and it is judged in the same way by the four outcome statuses, the positive criterion, and the null-conclusion criterion. Source-domain materials can only propose candidates for the target end. Without independent support at the target end, the conclusion remains “a mapping awaiting testing” or “unknown.”

5.9Note

Understanding this section

5.9 Evidential boundaries and independent support

Labeling a transformation “Aggregation” or “Compression or Abstraction” states only which rules will guide the question. The target object's properties require its own material; source-object success or procedural self-claims cannot fill the gaps.

The names, numbers, summaries of meaning, and classification results of the nine scale transformations specify modes of description and testing. They are not empirical observations that “a transformation occurred,” “the mapping is valid,” or “the target property holds.” Conceptual explanations clarify questions but cannot be inserted as object material into the evidence at the source end or the target end.

Internal examples and formula proofs have their own uses: showing logical possibilities, counterexamples, or conditional derivations without observing actual objects. How completely the items are filled in, and results reported by the algorithm itself, likewise cannot replace object grounds. An algorithm's result may be an output to check; correctness requires recalculation against independently checkable source/target material and rules, not self-validation through its own “passed” label.

Every actual transformation must separately check source and target: what source material supports, what target material observes, how the ends map, what is preserved, changed, or lost, the size of errors, and competing explanations. Repeated naming cannot turn one object's material into independent support for another.

Independent support is neither saving one report as two files nor requiring statistical independence of all source/target material. The minimum responsibility is verifiable object grounds at both ends, without internal labels serving as circular evidence. If a particular claim additionally needs out-of-sample evaluation, independent replication, proportionate intervention, or a statistically independent design, add those requirements for that claim. Shared sources and dependencies must be disclosed.

Evidence status follows the same four outcome statuses and criteria. A descriptive mapping actually passing its rules may be “supported”; empirical tests, causation, or conversion still require corresponding formal tests. An unevaluated target side is “not yet evaluated”; evaluated but insufficient bridging or support is “not supported or unresolved.” A bounded null conclusion also requires independent target material, a predetermined null-conclusion rule, and equivalence/sufficiency, power/sensitivity, and tolerance checks. “No target evidence found” cannot directly yield “null conclusion supported.”

Support in the source domain generates only a target candidate. An unresolved target does not automatically overturn the source conclusion, nor must a failed target mapping negate measured source properties. Retain local accomplishments and precisely limit transfer scope, rather than compress the whole study into entirely true or entirely false.

The property being compared also matters. Cost-calibration material supports cost calibration, not automatically adequate representation of health needs. Preserving one statistic does not guarantee another task. If source-to-target semantic correspondence is untested, a polished process cannot fill that factual gap.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    First specify whether the concrete claim concerns occurrence, mapping validity, a target property, or stronger causation/conversion. A transformation's name cannot substitute.

  2. 2

    List verifiable source-object and target-object material separately, disclose source dependencies, and exclude circular self-claims.

  3. 3

    Disclose preservation, change, loss, error, and target task in the mapping, checking for substituted properties.

  4. 4

    Review the mapping using actual target-object material, comparing competing explanations and evidence of failure.

  5. 5

    Determine status according to actual execution in the selected mode, the positive criterion, and the independent null-conclusion criterion.

  6. 6

    When target support is insufficient, stop at candidate or unknown status while retaining independently supported source conclusions.

  7. 7

    New calculations may improve understanding, but repeatedly processing the same material cannot count as new real observations.

Distinctions to keep clear

Semantic signature

Specifies how to describe and test an operation.

≠

Empirical support

The object's own material supports specific facts and bounded relations.

Output of an algorithm

A checkable computational result.

≠

An algorithm's claim to be correct

A label cannot replace checking output against the object.

Two files

May be copies or retellings of the same data.

≠

Independent support at both ends

Material supporting source/target claims respectively, with transparent dependencies.

Established source conclusion

Valid for the original object and conditions.

≠

Established target conclusion

Requires corresponding target grounds; it cannot be automatically transferred.

Mathematical construction: a correct source mean does not ensure a correct target outputTeaching scenario

AssumptionsA complete finite three-number task with equal weights and no missingness. Target 5 is an explicitly fictional error example.

Fictional source records are (2,4,6). The predetermined aggregation rule for the mean gives (2+4+6)/3=4, but the target report says 5 with “aggregation, supported, validation passed.” Independent examination of the target output reveals that 5 violates the rule; complete labels cannot correct the value. If the target report has not been obtained and only the program's claim to have output 4 is known, the actual output and provenance still need checking. Source-side calculation does not establish correct target delivery.

BoundaryFormal calculation can show this example table violates the rule; it cannot evaluate any real software or organization.

Teaching construction: separate repeated processing from new target observationTeaching scenario

AssumptionsReport, devices, and window are teaching assumptions; the summary introduces no new measurement.

Suppose source report R describes device A's behavior during window W, and summary S merely rewrites R into a few sentences. Listing R as evidence at the source end and S as evidence at the target end does not prove another device B behaves similarly. If the target task is checking summary fidelity, R and S are indeed the outputs to compare at the two ends. If it concerns B's behavior, observations of B itself remain necessary.

BoundaryThe same file pair has different support scope for different tasks. Independence is not judged simply by file count.

Conditional construction: retain status when target material is missingTeaching scenario

AssumptionsAssumes a bounded source conclusion without inventing a study name or numbers for it. Target gaps are stated individually.

Suppose a source-domain propagation rule is supported under its own design, while the target domain has only a proposed network of the same form, with delays, capacities, and alternative routes unmeasured. If the target branch has not been carried out, record “not yet evaluated.” If investigation occurred but key paths remain uncheckable, “not supported or unresolved” may apply. Neither supports a null conclusion of “no propagation in the target.”

BoundaryDemonstrates status logic only, without issuing a conclusion for any actual target.

Obermeyer and colleagues use target-health material to check a proxy labelDocumented case

The 2019 study found that the audited algorithm predicted healthcare costs. At the same risk score, subsequent costs were broadly similar across the two groups, but health burdens differed markedly. The study used actual health indicators rather than concluding from the cost label or score name alone that “health needs were represented.” This section's additional observation is that validation of a claimed target property requires corresponding material.

SourceObermeyer et al.（2019），Dissecting racial bias in an algorithm used to manage the health of populationsScience 366, printed pp.449–450, Mechanism of bias and adjacent text on health differencesReading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsIllustrates only cross-group cost calibration and health differences in the study's objects. Similar calibration does not mean low individual or overall prediction error. No patient advice is given, and no eligibility for any transformation or formal test is awarded retroactively.

Read the case and sources

What it limitsThe definition did not observe that summary. Check source/target content and queries.

What does not follow

  • Do not misread independent support as statistical independence for all material. Choose a proportionate evidential design for the specific claim.
  • Missing target material means unknown or unevaluated, not proof that the target property is absent.
  • Retain formal proofs' conditional validity and domain studies' own conclusions without retroactively granting eligibility as a formal test.
  • One erroneous output does not make every algorithmic result wrong. Repair must locate the specific input, mapping, rule, or execution failure.
  • The teaching example's target file and numbers are artificially given, not claimed read from a real system.

Scope and open questions

The original study directly examines differences between proxy predictions and the claimed target, illustrating why items/labels cannot replace target material. It is not presented as a formal scale record.

Which step between source (2,4,6) and target 5 can be directly checked?

The equal-weight rule gives 4, so target 5 is inconsistent. The “supported” label cannot offset the arithmetic conflict.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Can R and summary S serve as material for the two ends?

For summary fidelity, source and target outputs may be checked separately. For another real object B's behavior, S cannot substitute for observing B.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Does a result reported by an algorithm itself have any use?

It may serve as an output to check or a claim about execution. A self-claim of correctness cannot replace substantive checking and independent object material.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Why does an unmeasured target not receive bounded null support?

Because null support also requires target material and the predetermined three criteria of equivalence/sufficiency, power/sensitivity, and tolerance. Unknown is not zero.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If target transfer fails, must the source study also be invalidated?

Not necessarily. Locate the target mapping or condition gap while retaining the source conclusion's independent eligibility within its original scope.
